transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2025-05-14 09:00 PT | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Nina Gomez (Redwood SE), Olga Ruiz (Redwood CSM), James Park (Catalyst Eng Lead), Maya Singh (Catalyst Security Lead), Tom Liu (Catalyst PM), Rita Alvarez (Catalyst DevOps)

[00:00] Samir: ok folks, thanks for joining, uh we'll kick off, this is the weekly pilot sync focused on the compliance gate items for the Catalyst Health POC. Um Nina and I will run through the outstanding asks.
[00:22] James: hey yeah thanks, quick note we also have a question about the retention window for audit logs before we dig in.
[00:35] Nina: yep, great, so quick agenda, SOC2 artifacts, SSO + SCIM provisioning with Okta, audit log export and retention, data deletion flows during the pilot, and then short results recap and next steps.
[00:50] Maya: sounds good, just flagging that Catalyst needs 90 days of immutable logs for the initial review, and we also want field-level visibility for user ids and tenant ids.
[01:05] Nina: got it, right now default retention on the hosted trial is 30 days, but we can enable extended retention for pilot customers and do an export to your S3 bucket or to your SIEM. We can also do real-time forwarding via our audit webhook.
[01:25] Tom: when you say export to S3, is that historical backfill or continuous stream?
[01:31] Nina: both — you can do a backfill of the last 30 days and provision a continuous daily export. The export files are gzipped ndjson with a schema we will share.
[01:43] Samir: note — sometimes the console label shows "Reedwood Console" in the transcript hah, ignore that, it's 'Redwood Console'.
[01:55] Rita: haha yeah ok. Practical question on PII, we are sending some PHI tokens in request payloads to the endpoint, what's the recommended approach during the POC?
[02:07] Nina: good question. For PHI we recommend pseudonymization on the client side where possible. For fields that must be sent, we have scoped data handling in our private option; in hosted mode we can enable stricter retention and disable analytics for the pilot. Also we provide a data deletion endpoint and a documented retention policy.
[02:28] Maya: will the deletion endpoint purge everything from backups as well? We need the deletion to be defensible for audits.
[02:35] Nina: yes, we have a documented retention workflow: primary store delete, then mark for removal from backups on a 90-day cycle. For SOC2 evidence we can provide our deletion playbook and the attestations. (slight hesitation) I'll attach the exact excerpt.
[02:55] James: ok that helps. On SSO, we use Okta and need SCIM for group provisioning. What do you support?
[03:04] Samir: we support SCIM 2.0, Okta out-of-the-box. We can do one-way provisioning (Okta -> Redwood) and sync groups/roles; we also support SAML or OIDC for SSO depending on your preference.
[03:20] Maya: do you support SCIM user deprovisioning to trigger immediate cert revocation on the Redwood side?
[03:26] Nina: yes, we honor deprovision events; deprovision triggers immediate role removal and token revocation. There's a small window if someone has a live token, but tokens are short-lived by default and we can revoke sessions programmatically.
[03:40] Tom: slightly unrelated, any RBAC finer-grained capabilities? We need feature access per role and limited admin views.
[03:46] Nina: yep RBAC supports admin, developer, observer roles and you can create custom roles via our console — I'll note that custom role creation requires a config flag in the pilot.
[04:00] [crosstalk] Maya: ok.
[04:05] James: quick POC results note — we've been running the model for two days, average p50 latency is ~180ms for our baseline prompts, p95 is around 420ms when we hit batch spikes, tokens per request are about 120. Those numbers are from our internal harness.
[04:22] Samir: thanks, those are in line with what we saw in the dev region. For the Dedicated path we can tighten p95 via reserved capacity; but for the pilot you can tune batching, KV cache and the sequence length to reduce tokens.
[04:40] James: KV cache? (mumble) K V cash?
[04:44] Nina: yeah K V cache — key value cache, sorry the transcript sometimes splits those letters — it helps with repeated context.
[04:51] Maya: back to compliance: SOC2 Type II — do you have a public report we can reference and a process to get the more detailed auditor pack?
[05:00] Samir: yes we have the SOC2 Type II and the auditor pack. I'll share the redacted pack and a pointer to the vendor that did our audit. We'll also provide the controls matrix and the network diagram.
[05:12] Maya: good. Also need clarity on encryption at rest and KMS. We use a customer-managed key expectation for production, but for POC we need to know if our data is encrypted with provider-managed keys or if you can bring-your-own-key (BYOK).
[05:28] Nina: for hosted POC by default it's provider-managed KMS; we offer BYOK and HSM-backed keys on Dedicated and Private deployments. For pilot, we can demo BYOK in a sandbox but it's typically gated behind an NDA/contract.
[05:44] Rita: do you have logs showing who accessed which data (user-level audit trails)?
[05:49] Nina: yes audit events include actor, action, resource, timestamp, request id, and tenant id. We will confirm the exact field names; Maya you mentioned a list of must-have fields — if you send that we'll map them to our schema.
[06:04] Maya: will do.
[06:07] [pause]
[06:10] Tom: about the export format, you mentioned ndjson gz — can we get a sample file?
[06:15] Nina: yes, I'll drop a sample in the shared drive; expect it with the schema and a small parser example.
[06:23] Samir: quick note on the SOC2 data residency question — are you operating in us-east and eu-west?
[06:29] James: Catalyst is on US region for now, but we may need EU later.
[06:34] Samir: we can pin region for the pilot endpoints to us-east and ensure logs and backups live there. We'll note the cross-region replication rules.
[06:45] Maya: ping on third-party subprocessors — we need the list for our legal team.
[06:50] Samir: yes, legal pack will include subprocessors list.
[06:53] Nina: also, a small note — the console can show token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency, which your infra folks liked in the trial. (laugh)
[07:03] James: yea that's been helpful.
[07:07] Maya: one more thing: for defensible deletion, we need the retention SLA documented in the contract.
[07:12] Samir: understood, we'll include retention SLAs in the pilot addendum.
[07:17] Rita: about SSO test — what's the quickest path? Okta metadata or OIDC discovery?
[07:22] Nina: Okta metadata is quickest. If you can provision a test app in your Okta tenant and send the metadata URL, we will configure SCIM on our side and push a few test users. For group mapping we support attribute mapping to roles.
[07:37] [00:38] Maya: will the SCIM push include custom attributes like "clinician_id"?
[07:42] Nina: yes custom attributes are supported, you'll need to list the attributes in the SCIM mapping.
[07:47] Samir: let's loop in engineering: Rita will provide Okta details, Nina will do the SCIM provisioning, and Samir will send the SOC2 pack.
[07:57] James: timeline question — after we enable SCIM and logs, how long until we can consider the compliance gate satisfied for the pilot?
[08:06] Maya: and who signs off?
[08:09] Samir: typically sign-off requires SOC2 artifacts delivered, SCIM provisioned with at least one test user and group mapping, and audit-log exports verified to your S3; security lead (Maya) would sign off for the pilot. We can aim for sign-off by 2025-05-22 if items complete.
[08:26] Maya: sounds reasonable.
[08:29] [pause]
[08:32] Tom: anything else on performance tuning during the pilot? We might want a short SE session to tune batch parameters.
[08:39] Nina: yes, we can schedule a 60-minute tuning session next week — we'll look at prompt templates, batching, and KV cache warmups.
[08:48] Samir: ok I'll propose two slots.
[08:51] [wrap] Samir: recap of action items: I will send SOC2 + security pack; Nina will enable audit export to your sandbox S3 and send sample schema; Rita to provide Okta test tenant; Maya to send required audit fields; schedule encryption deep dive — Olga will help coordinate. Any final comments?
[09:09] Maya: none from me, thanks.
[09:11] James: thanks everyone.
[09:13] Samir: great, thanks all — we'll follow up in Slack with the links and timeline.

End of transcript.
